newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cerebos shares plunge, earnings downgraded.
newsitem.headline: Cerebos shares plunge, earnings downgraded.

text.p: Food-based Cerebos Pacific Ltd was hit by a sell-off on Wednesday as analysts downgraded the company after it reported poorer than expect first half profits and said it expected a tougher second half.
Cerebos shares sank to a 42-month low of Singapore $6.45 in mid-afternoon trading on Wednesday. Volume was over two million shares.
The last time the shares were traded at S$6.45 was on October 8, 1993.

Several broking firms have lowered their full-year earnings forecast for the group. Prior to the release of the interim results, the concensus forecast earnings for the group in 1997 was a 11 percent rise to S$113.5 million, according to the Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate Directory.
Cerebos, which is 84.1 percent controlled by Japan's Suntory Pacific, reported flat profits of S$47.01 million for the six months ended March 31 1997. Turnover fell three percent to S$338.10 million.
"I expect the negative momentum on the group sales to continue in the second half," Ong said. Soc-Gen Crosby has a sell on Cerebos.
Vickers Ballas analyst Terence Tan revised down his full year earnings projection for the group by 12 percent to around S$99 million.
"Prior to the results announcement, expectations were for a double digit growth. Now, we are expecting full year to be slightly negative," Tan said.
The group blamed slowing economies in Asia, weak credit conditions in China and the termination of a distribution agreement in Australia for its poor showing.

Analysts had mostly expected the company, which makes Brand's chicken essence and had reported double digit growth since the early 1990s, to report at least some growth growth in the first half after its 11 percent rise in earnings in 1996.
"The results are quite bad. But there is no quick fix to their problems," said Michael Ong, an investment analyst with Soc-Gen Crosby.
Some analysts said that given the poor earnings outlook, a fair value for the Cerebos, which still has a cash pile of about S$120 million, could be around S$6.40.

But Ong said the technicals for the stock looked quite weak after it broke support at S$8. "It is a rather illiquid stock with major shareholder Suntory holding more than 84 percent. This could result in quite volatile movements on the way down."
